targetGroup: Students studying in Grades 9-12 across ICSE, CBSE, ISC and State Boards
assessmentPurpose: To help students discover hidden strengths, behavioural tendencies, interests, thinking style, work style, motivation, leadership potential, entrepreneurial mindset, emotional intelligence, AI readiness and future career suitability — across an expanded set of 19 career clusters including sports, defence, agriculture, hospitality, architecture, finance and skilled trades.
assessmentDisclaimer: CareerDNA is an exploratory career-guidance assessment. It does not diagnose personality, determine ability, or prescribe a single career. Results should be discussed with the student and, where appropriate, a qualified counsellor.
studentInstructions: Read each question carefully and choose the response that feels closest to how you would naturally think, feel or act. Do not choose what sounds ideal. Choose what feels most true for you.

scoringModel.scoreType: Competency-based weighted scoring with preference-context signals
scoringModel.rankingQuestionScoring: Ipsative: only relative order within the same ranking question is interpreted.
scoringModel.reflectionQuestionScoring: Qualitative and unscored in Phase 1; word count is a completion check, not a quality score.
scoringModel.forcedChoiceScoring: Each option maps to different competency signals; no option should be treated as universally correct
scoringModel.situationalJudgementScoring: Options should be scored based on behavioural maturity, competency relevance and career-fit signal
scoringModel.optionLevelScoring: Option weights are used for ordered Likert and situational-judgement items. Forced-choice, ranking and context items are interpreted as preferences, not universally good or bad answers.

scoringClasses.competencyEvidence: Differentiated option weights contribute to competency scores.
scoringClasses.selfReportSignal: Self-report signal; interpret alongside behavioural and scenario evidence.
scoringClasses.preferenceSignal: Career, work-environment or value preference; maps to exploration directions, not a better/worse score.
scoringClasses.experienceEvidence: Reported exposure or behaviour; used to describe evidence coverage, not ability.
scoringClasses.qualitativeEvidence: Open response for counsellor review; unscored in Phase 1.
scoringClasses.validityCheck: Used only to estimate response confidence; never shown as a career or personality score.

scoringModel.calibrationPolicy: An item may contribute to a competency score only when it has explicit differentiated optionWeights. Items without them are classified and reported without inferred competency scoring.
scoringModel.taxonomyPolicy: All hiddenCompetencies and optionWeights must use names from competencyFramework after normalization.

Emerging.interpretation: The student may still be developing this competency or may not naturally prefer situations requiring it.

Developing.interpretation: The student shows some positive signals but may need practice, exposure or guidance.

Strong.interpretation: The student shows consistent strength or interest in this competency area.

Exceptional.interpretation: The student shows very strong and repeated signals in this competency area.

validityFlags.tooManyNeutralResponses: May indicate low engagement or uncertainty
validityFlags.veryFastCompletion: May indicate random or careless answering
validityFlags.lowReflectionDetail: May indicate low engagement in open-ended questions

grades9to10.focus: Broad exploration. Keep every stream open and collect real experiences before choosing subjects in Class 11.
actions: Try one taster activity per term from your top three clusters (club, online course, or project).
Talk to one adult per month who works in a field that interests you.
Keep a portfolio of projects, competitions and certificates.
Do not lock a stream based on this report alone; revisit after Class 10 results.
grades9to10.message: Your results are directions to explore, not decisions to make. Use Classes 9 and 10 to test ideas cheaply.

grades11to12.focus: Convergence. Combine your stream with your top clusters to shortlist degrees, exams and first steps.
actions: Shortlist 2-3 careers from your top clusters and research their entrance exams and colleges.
Start one deep project or internship aligned with your strongest cluster.
Map required subjects and exams against your current stream; identify gaps early.
Discuss the Parent/Counsellor Notes section with your family before finalising applications.
grades11to12.message: Use your top clusters to choose degrees and exams deliberately — and remember adjacent clusters often hide the best-fit careers.
